questions.question: Define stratified, systematic, and cluster sampling. How are they different from simple random sampling? .
questions.solution_html:
• Randomness is crucial in cluster sampling to ensure unbiased representation of the
  • population. It ensures unbiased representation and improves generalizability of results.
  • Reduces selection bias: Randomly selecting clusters prevents researchers from
  • choosing groups that may skew results.
  • Improves generalizability: It helps ensure that findings from the sample can be
  • applied to the broader population.
  • Maintains statistical validity: Random selection supports the use of probability
  • theory for estimating sampling errors and confidence intervals.
  • Enhances diversity: Random clusters are more likely to capture varied
  • characteristics across the population.
